basis: Closed vocabularies for the qualitative layer. Their only job is to stop the model inventing a new label for every call, so two calls can be compared and the UI can filter. Nothing here is scored - see sales_framework.json for anything that produces a number.
evidence_rule: A signal, technique, objection, need or buying signal is only reported when it is supported by transcript evidence that resolves to a real segment. evidence.py drops anything that does not, so an unsupported label cannot reach the report. Do not relax this in the prompt.

customer_signals.note: Signals expressed by the customer or another non-representative participant.

types.label: Buying intent
types.definition: The customer indicates they want to move forward - asking about price, start dates, enrolment or next steps in a possessive way.

types.label: Hesitation
types.definition: The customer stalls, defers, or asks for time without committing.

types.label: Price sensitivity
types.definition: The customer reacts to cost, asks for discounts, instalments, or compares on price.

types.label: Trust or scepticism
types.definition: The customer expresses confidence in, or doubt about, the brand, the representative or the claims made.

types.label: Decision authority
types.definition: The customer reveals who decides - themselves alone, a partner, family, a manager or a committee.

types.label: Objection
types.definition: The customer raises a concern that stands between them and a purchase.

types.label: Engagement
types.definition: The customer participates actively - asking questions, elaborating, building on what was said.

types.label: Interest
types.definition: The customer expresses positive attention to a specific benefit, feature or outcome.

types.label: Confusion
types.definition: The customer misunderstands something or asks for the same point to be repeated or clarified.

types.label: Risk concern
types.definition: The customer worries about what happens if it does not work - refunds, guarantees, time wasted, reputation.

types.label: Urgency
types.definition: The customer expresses their own time pressure or a deadline of their own.

types.label: Commitment
types.definition: The customer agrees to do something specific - pay, attend, send documents, join a session.

types.label: Next-step readiness
types.definition: The customer accepts or proposes a concrete next action.

types.label: Emotional motivation
types.definition: The customer reveals the personal driver behind the purchase - status, security, family, frustration, ambition.

types.label: Disengagement
types.definition: The customer withdraws - short answers, wanting to end the call, no reciprocal questions.

rep_techniques.note: Persuasion techniques used by the sales representative. Reported with an effectiveness read, never scored on their own.

types.label: Social proof
types.definition: Cites other customers, cohort sizes, testimonials or peer behaviour.

types.label: Authority
types.definition: Cites credentials, faculty, accreditation, rankings or institutional standing.

types.label: Scarcity or urgency
types.definition: Cites limited seats, closing dates, expiring pricing or a cohort start.

types.label: Loss aversion
types.definition: Frames the cost of not acting - opportunities missed, stagnation, competitors moving ahead.

types.label: Value framing
types.definition: Reframes price against outcome, ROI, instalments or a per-unit comparison.

types.label: Reciprocity
types.definition: Offers something first - a resource, a review, a free session, extra access.

types.label: Commitment and consistency
types.definition: Secures a small agreement and builds on it toward a larger one.

types.label: Risk reversal
types.definition: Removes perceived risk - guarantees, refunds, trial periods, staged payments.

types.label: Personalisation
types.definition: Ties the offer to this customer's stated situation, goal or constraint.

types.label: Storytelling
types.definition: Uses a narrative about a comparable customer to carry the point.

effectiveness.note: How the customer actually responded to a technique, read from what they said next - not from whether the technique is generally considered good practice.

pitch_structures.note: There is no single correct pitch structure. The structure is identified, then assessed for fit with THIS customer, product, price band and awareness level.

types.label: Consultative (discovery first)
types.definition: Extensive questioning before any solution is presented.

types.label: Problem-solution
types.definition: Names the problem, agitates it, then presents the product as the resolution.

types.label: Story-led
types.definition: Leads with a narrative of a comparable customer's journey.

types.label: ROI-led
types.definition: Leads with outcomes, returns and payback.

types.label: Feature-led
types.definition: Walks through the product's components and specifications.

types.label: Social-proof-led
types.definition: Leads with who else has bought and what happened to them.

types.label: Comparison-led
types.definition: Positions primarily against alternatives or competitors.

types.label: Direct offer
types.definition: Moves quickly to the offer and the close with minimal build-up.

types.label: Mixed
types.definition: Combines several structures without one dominating.

types.label: No discernible structure
types.definition: No recognisable structure was followed.

context_factors.note: Factors the analysis may take into account when judging whether the representative adapted to THIS customer. They are contextual signals, never deterministic rules: nothing here licenses a claim about how people from a region or profile behave. A factor is only used when the call context actually supplies it.
factors: call direction and stage of the journey

limits.note: Caps exist to bound prompt output size and to discourage padding. They are ceilings, not targets - the report shows however many are genuinely supported, and report.py never pads to reach a number.
